Subject: Interest in Optimizer Toolkit — pilot packaging and economics

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — the batching and KV cache approach looks promising for our real-time summarization pipeline. Procurement asked me to get a clear picture of pricing for a 3-month pilot (approx 1.5M tokens/month) and any one-time engineering credits you typically provide for quantization/engineering work.

A few specific asks:
- Example pricing for pilot vs committed monthly volume (1.5M tokens) and the expected per-token delta when using the optimizer toolkit (batching+cache) vs standard hosted model.
- Any recommended quantization profile you’d suggest for a TGI-style LLM we’ll be running (model: open-instruct-22B) and whether Redwood supports mixed-precision rollouts.
- Typical billing mechanics for credits and how they appear on invoices.

We’ve attached our security questionnaire (summarized) — procurement will pull in legal once economics are close. Can someone on your team share a one-pager and a pricing worksheet we can run internally?

Best,
Elena
Director of ML Ops
BrightWave Analytics

Hi Elena — thanks for the notes and the security doc. Looping in Connor (inference eng) and Jonas (commercial) to put concrete numbers behind this.

High level answers first:
- Pilot structure we recommend: 3-month pilot with a trial credit pool applied to inbound tokens and a discounted committed-month rate if you convert to a rolling 12-month reserved commitment. For 1.5M tokens/month, pilot pricing estimate is attached (see optimizer-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx) — the optimizer toolkit (batching + KV cache + three-tier quantization) typically reduces billed token-equivalent spend by 25–45% depending on prefix overlap and latency SLOs.
- Quantization recommendation: start with INT8-AVX fallback on non-critical tails and a dynamic FP16 path for quality-sensitive routes; Connor to confirm specifics for the open-instruct-22B profile. Redwood supports staged rollouts and mixed-precision; we can deliver a short engineering sweep as part of the pilot credits.
- Credits: labeled as "technical credits" on billing; they offset usage through the pilot period and any unused credits are applied only if you convert to a committed plan within 30 days of pilot end.

Next steps I propose:
1) Connor to provide a concise tech note on the quantization/latency tradeoffs for open-instruct-22B.
2) Jonas to propose a pilot commercial sketch with a one-time engineering credit and conversion pricing.
3) We’ll share a one-pager and the pricing worksheet you requested.

Is procurement ok with a short-term SOW for the engineering sweep, or do you prefer credits only?

—Mina
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: optimizer-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx

Hi Elena, Mina — quick technical note to make the numbers actionable.

Summary (short):
- For open-instruct-22B we recommend starting with QAT->INT8 for encoder layers and FP16 for the last decoder block to preserve generation fidelity. In our production profiles this gives ~2.8x inference throughput improvement and roughly ~38% token-cost reduction in typical conversational patterns where you get prefix reuse.
- Batching policy: for a 1.5M tokens/month workload with peak qps of ~35, configure a dynamic batching window of 12–20ms with max batch size 96 on p4d-class hosts; this trades a few ms for 18–22% additional throughput on average.
- KV cache caching: enable prefix caching for any repeated session-level prompts; for BrightWave’s summarization use-case we expect 12–16% extra savings beyond batching alone.

Engineering credit scope (recommendation):
- 10 dedicated engineering-hours for initial quantization sweep + 8 hours for validation and A/B quality checks. If you prefer a scoped SOW, we can convert that to a fixed-price line item.

I’ll drop a 1-page tech note into the shared drive and attach a simple perf sketch to the pricing sheet.

—Connor
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: perf-sketch-open-instruct-22B.pdf
